topic: Kinematic theory of rapid movements: lognormal velocity profiles

design_implication: Represent the user's letters as lognormal strokes for synthesis from few samples

topic: Tremor estimation: two-stage voluntary/tremor separation with WFLC and Kalman filtering (gyroscopes)

topic: Kalman-network hybrid (learned Kalman gain)

topic: Fixed-lag smoothing: RTS backward recursion with stored gains
citation: Sarkka S. Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing. Cambridge University Press (IMS Textbooks 3), s10.5 General fixed-lag smoother equations, Algorithm 10.7
task_or_setup: Gaussian fixed-lag smoother: store the filter's smoothing gains during prediction, then per time step run the RTS backward recursion over the lag window

transferability_reason: Standard estimation theory; the pen needs only the linear-Gaussian case
design_implication: Use the stored-gain RTS form on the pen MCU; cost grows with the lag (bounded here to 100 ms)

citation: Annett M, Ng A, Dietz P, Bischof WF, Gupta A. How low should we go? Understanding the perception of latency while inking. Graphics Interface 2014, pp 167-174
task_or_setup: High-performance stylus system (about 1 ms base latency); JND against a 7 ms baseline while drawing a line, writing 'party' and drawing a star (Exp 1); nib-ink offsets and hand visibility (Exp 2)
key_quantitative_findings: JND median 53 ms line (range 31-76), 50 ms writing 'party' (32-87), 61 ms star (21-82), 53 ms over tasks (task n.s.); Exp 2: hand and stylus visible Mdn 59 ms (33-104) vs hidden 97 ms (59-105), p < 0.005; displayed ink offsets 0/6.5/65 mm had no significant effect; commercial devices 60-120 ms
locator: s4.5 Results (Exp 1); s5 Results (Exp 2); Figures 3 and 5
limitations: Tablet display, not paper; n = 12 per experiment
relevance_to_design: What a writer sees with delayed ink: the hand and pen move ahead and the ink follows; about half of writers notice 50 ms
transferability_reason: Same perceptual question (ink trailing the pen), different surface
design_implication: Keep the ink lag at or below about 25-50 ms; treat 100 ms as noticeable by nearly everyone

topic: Delayed visual feedback in handwriting: stroke duplication errors
citation: Tamada T. Effects of delayed visual feedback on handwriting. Japanese Psychological Research 37(2):103-109
task_or_setup: Handwriting with visual feedback delayed 0, 33, 67, 100, 133, 167, 267 and 500 ms
participants_or_bench: Participants (number not in the abstract read)
key_quantitative_findings: Error rates rose with delay; addition errors (stroke duplication, 'feeeling'), where a set of strokes repeats; visual monitoring indispensable for repetitive letters (abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; whole visual scene delayed (video), not ink alone
relevance_to_design: A lagging ink could cause repeated strokes and letters in writers who rely on seeing their ink (m, n, u, w, e)
transferability_reason: Delay of the whole visual feedback, not of ink behind a visible hand
design_implication: Test delayed ink for letter duplication errors (EXP-L02)

topic: Delayed visual feedback in handwriting (Kanji and English)
citation: Morikiyo Y, Matsushima T. Effects of delayed visual feedback on motor control performance. Perceptual and Motor Skills 70(1):111-114
task_or_setup: Writing Kanji and English with visual feedback delayed 200, 500, 767 and 1000 ms
key_quantitative_findings: Large decrement with delay; errors were insertion of line elements and letter duplication; letter size increased with delay (abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; delays of 200 ms and more
relevance_to_design: Upper bound: at 200 ms and above handwriting breaks down
transferability_reason: Whole-scene video delay
design_implication: Never let the ink lag exceed 100 ms

topic: Delayed visual feedback on visual-motor tasks (early study)
citation: Smith WM, McCrary JW, Smith KU. Delayed visual feedback and behavior. Science 132(3433):1013-1014
task_or_setup: Video-tape delay of visual feedback during simple visual-motor tasks
key_quantitative_findings: Effects 'marked and deleterious', similar to delayed auditory feedback (abstract; delay value not in the abstract)
relevance_to_design: Historical basis for the risk of lagged visual feedback
transferability_reason: Old video method; delay not stated in the abstract
design_implication: Supports measuring writers' errors under ink lag rather than assuming adaptation

topic: Assist-as-needed with a forgetting factor and an error deadband (optimisation of error and assistance)
citation: Emken JL, Benitez R, Reinkensmeyer DJ. Human-robot cooperative movement training: learning a novel sensory motor transformation during walking with robotic assistance-as-needed. J Neuroeng Rehabil 4:8
task_or_setup: Robotic force-field 'virtual impairment' on the left leg during treadmill walking; AAN trainer derived from minimising error plus assistance
key_quantitative_findings: Optimal trainer = error-based controller with a forgetting factor; an error weighting (deadband) lets assistance fade to zero despite natural variability; 'the robot must relax its assistance at a rate faster than that of the learning human' (abstract)
relevance_to_design: Exact form of the per-letter guidance gain law here: g(k+1) = f g(k) + kappa (e(k) - e_tol)+
transferability_reason: Different limb and task; same learning principle
design_implication: Use a forgetting factor f < 1 and a tolerance band so help fades; fade faster than the writer learns

topic: Deep RL for tremor suppression in simulation (soft exoskeleton, PD)
citation: Endrei T, Foldi S, Makk A, Cserey G. Learning to suppress tremors: a deep reinforcement learning-enabled soft exoskeleton for Parkinson's patients. Front Robot AI 12:1537470
task_or_setup: PyBullet + Gym arm model (7 DoF); tremor = two sines + noise; TD7 agent; domain randomisation 4-12 Hz, amplitude 0.1-1.0, anatomy 0.9-1.1x
key_quantitative_findings: More than 99 % tremor amplitude suppression in simulation; the observation includes the tremor torques; no sim-to-real test
limitations: Privileged observation (tremor torques) and simulation only
relevance_to_design: Shows how easily RL results look perfect when the policy observes the tremor; the policies here see only the pen's sensors
transferability_reason: Privileged observations; no hardware
design_implication: Report RL only with the sensors the pen has, on held-out writers and seeds

topic: ET spiral analysis: tremor from tablet pen positions (clinical validation)
citation: Haubenberger D, Kalowitz D, Nahab FB, Toro C, Ippolito D, Luckenbaugh DA, Wittevrongel L, Hallett M. Validation of digital spiral analysis as outcome parameter for clinical trials in essential tremor. Mov Disord 26(11):2073-2080
task_or_setup: Digitising-tablet spirals; tremor severity from the velocity-spectrum tremor peak (FFT of pen-tip positions); ethanol challenge
key_quantitative_findings: Correlated with visual ratings (P < 0.0001) and more sensitive to the ethanol effect (P < 0.05) (abstract)
relevance_to_design: Supports a tremor-line (spectral peak) detector on pen-tip data as the pen's gate
transferability_reason: ET, tablet pen tip
design_implication: The pen can calibrate and log tremor from its own page sensor in the same way

topic: Tremor-line detector gate: open fraction by condition and on tremor-free writing (test writers)
citation: This ledger's calculation: ai2 (study L, AI and control v2), aiguide test writers 0-5 x seeds 200-203; detector r_on 5, r_off 2.5, 4 s window
task_or_setup: aiguide test writers 0-5 x seeds 200-203; detector r_on 5, r_off 2.5, 4 s window
key_quantitative_findings: Gate open fraction (mean over writers and seeds): tremor-free 0.000; 6 Hz 0.3/1/2 mm 0.00/0.51/0.71; 8 Hz 0.03/0.72/0.73; 10 Hz 0.13/0.73/0.73 (includes the 4.5 s start-up of each 20 s recording)
limitations: Synthetic tremor with fixed frequency per recording
relevance_to_design: The gate is what keeps tremor-free writing untouched
transferability_reason: Simulation on synthetic glyph writers, synthetic tremor and assumed hand, grip, sensor and device parameters (model HW1); not a measurement
design_implication: Keep the detector state across lines in a session so the start-up is paid once

topic: Causal gated listening tracker (model-based stack) vs the Rev H tracker, by tremor frequency
citation: This ledger's calculation: ai2 (study L, AI and control v2), aiguide test writers 0-5 x seeds 200-203 x 6/8/10 Hz x 0.3/1/2 mm
task_or_setup: aiguide test writers 0-5 x seeds 200-203 x 6/8/10 Hz x 0.3/1/2 mm
comparator: Rev H tracker (as built) on the same runs
key_quantitative_findings: Ink error 1-2 mm at 6/8/10 Hz: tracker 818/639/423 um, gated 540/426/325 um; 0.3 mm: tracker 162 um, gated 161 um; tremor-free moved: tracker 26.3 um, gated 26.3 um; paired gated - tracker ink 1-2 mm -197 um (95 % CI -206 to -188)
relevance_to_design: The biggest gain found here comes from listening harder only when a tremor line is present
transferability_reason: Simulation on synthetic glyph writers, synthetic tremor and assumed hand, grip, sensor and device parameters (model HW1); not a measurement
design_implication: Adopt as the Rev J firmware estimator (proposed DEC)

topic: Per-user calibration (20 s) of the learned estimator and closed-loop tuning check of learned and RL candidates
citation: This ledger's calculation: ai2 (study L, AI and control v2), aiguide tuning writers 100-103, seeds 300-301
task_or_setup: aiguide tuning writers 100-103, seeds 300-301
comparator: Rev H tracker (as built) on the same runs
key_quantitative_findings: Closed-loop tuning check (seeds 300-301, rules R1-R4 vs Rev H): passing ['gated', 'learned_ctx', 'learned_tcn']; adopted learned_tcn; gated J 419 um fc 33.5 um, learned_ctx J 293 um fc 21.1 um, learned_hybrid J 255 um fc 51.3 um, learned_tcn J 281 um fc 21.3 um, learned_transformer J 492 um fc 62.3 um, rl_arbiter J 297 um fc 60.9 um, rl_residual J 383 um fc 166.9 um
